newsitem.title: FRANCE: SWIMMING-VAN ALMSICK FEELS STRAIN AFTER LONG BREAK.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-VAN ALMSICK FEELS STRAIN AFTER LONG BREAK.

text.p: World champion Franziska van Almsick felt the strain on Sunday in only her second meeting since a four-month break from swimming following the 1996 Olympics.
"I have never used so much power to get such poor results," van Almsick said after losing the 100 metres freestyle to Michelle Smith of Ireland at the Sarcelles meeting near Paris.
Smith, a triple Olympic champion, won in 57.53 seconds with van Almsick second in 57.76. The German won the 50 metres freestyle, in which Smith did not race, in 27.01 seconds.
Van Almsick, who holds the long course world record in the 200 metres freestyle, is planning to defend her title at the Perth world championships in January.
"My big goal is the world championships, the 200 freestyle gold medal," said the German, who came second to Claudia Poll of Costa Rica in the Olympic final in Atlanta last year.
She said she was not ready to fully commit herself to the European championships in Seville in August.
"It's a bit too soon. I still have to qualify ... and there are other big names in the German team but if they need me in the relay I'll go."
Van Almsick, who returned to competition in a meeting in Magdeburg, Germany, in March, said she would go to the German championships next month but had not yet decided which events to enter.
"After four months my times are not so bad," said the 18-year-old German, who returned to training in early January following her break.
"I worked very hard for four years (between the 1992 Barcelona Olympics and the 1996 Atlanta Games) and I was fed up with training and needed some time to myself," she said.
"I needed a break but I found I couldn't stop for a year, so after four months I was back (in the pool) with a new trainer."
She said that during the break she went out in the evenings and saw friends a lot. "It was an easy life after Atlanta."
Smith confirmed she still wants to take part in the Sydney Games in 2000.
She brushed aside suggestions it would be tough in her late twenties, saying: "I broke two Irish records this weekend."
Her records were obtained in winning the 800 metres freestyle on Saturday and the 100 freestyle on Sunday. She also won the 200 medlay in two minutes 20.69 on Sunday.
Smith, in training since December, is not committing herself to either the Seville or Perth championships.
"I don't know when I'll decide," said Smith, whose next meeting is in Belgium in May. She also plans to participate in the Canet meeting in the south of France at the end of May.
